title: ML prioritization identifies two antimicrobial peptide candidates
summary: CalcAMP ranked 16,384 14-residue sequences in a researcher-defined LL-37-derived design space bounded by patent WO2015088344. Researchers selected GDST-038 and GDST-045 for laboratory tests; the paper reports activity against tested bacteria and elimination of detectable adherent S. aureus in a 3D human epidermal infection model at concentrations of at least 15 µM. Retro-inverso variants were prepared and tested after selection. These results do not establish human safety or clinical efficacy, and exact sequence-level patent priority remains open.
organization: Amsterdam University Medical Centre; Leiden University; Leiden University Medical Center

source_review.scope: Primary MDPI full article, abstract/results and author-affiliation block reviewed.

evidence.tested: The primary article reports in-vitro antimicrobial testing, biofilm assays and a 3D human epidermal infection model for selected parent/retro-inverso peptides.
evidence.unknown: These are in-vitro and tissue-model findings, not clinical efficacy or human safety. Sequence-level patent scope and independent replication are not established.
evidence.ai_role: CalcAMP ranked peptide sequences by predicted antimicrobial activity; researchers selected and experimentally tested two lead sequences and retro-inverso variants.
